塔馬克鼓是南亞次大陸桑塔爾人使用的膜鳴、無固定音高打擊樂器，屬於以鼓棒敲擊的雙面: The tamak' is a membranophone of indefinite pitch used by the Santal people of the South Asian subcontinent, a two-headed drum struck with drumsticks. Its body is of metal, in the shape of a large bowl, and its head is usually cowhide, about 14 to 18 inches across. The player strikes the two heads with a pair of sticks. The Santal believe it has a special religious power, and it is often used in religious ritual and festivals; its rhythm also gives Santal dance its basic beat and patterns, which makes it an important instrument of traditional music.
塔馬克鼓源於印度次大陸的桑塔爾人社群，是該民族傳統文化的重要象徵。這件金屬碗形鼓: The tamak' comes from the Santal community of the Indian subcontinent and is an important symbol of that people's traditional culture. This metal bowl-shaped drum gradually became the central instrument of religious ritual and folk celebration in Santal history. Generation after generation the Santal have woven the craft of making and playing the tamak' into daily life and spiritual belief. Over time its use has widened, from religious ritual to every kind of folk festival. Its distinctive cowhide head and precise rhythmic control make it the rhythmic foundation of Santal traditional dance. Through transmission between generations and exchange within the community its influence has gradually spread to neighbouring areas, becoming an important part of the diversity of Indian folk music and showing the Santal people's distinctive artistic creativity and cultural identity.

Its body is of metal, in the shape of a large bowl; the head is usually cowhide, about 14 to 18 inches across. It is played by striking the two heads with a pair of sticks, but the source does not state the material of the sticks, the kind of metal of the body, how the head is fixed, or any other structural part. It sounds when the sticks strike the cowhide head and set the membrane vibrating, producing rhythm.
塔馬克鼓音色渾厚而富有穿透力，具有溫暖的暗沉質感。其金屬鼓體與牛皮鼓面結合，產生: The tamak' has a deep, full tone that carries well, with a warm, dark quality. Its metal body and cowhide head together produce a clear, powerful low resonance; its range lies in the lower middle, and it is strong in rhythm and attack. The sound decays quickly when struck and has a clearly defined attack, which makes it good for marking the rhythmic edges of phrases. The metal body gives the sound a faint metallic quality, with more tension and edge than an all-wood drum. Its sound sits between a deep bass drum and a bright gong: it has the direct impact of percussion and the warmth of a resonant instrument, and that makes it an ideal rhythmic foundation in Santal music.
